title: Three Realms Convergence
next_chapter_hook: The double pupils of Chesspiece Number Forty-Nine opened completely, as if gazing at the final page of the ancient chess game—its voice rang out, carrying the weight of time beyond measure: 'You have finally arrived, Chen Ji. Or rather, I have waited for you precisely three thousand years.'

text.content: The rules of the Forbidden Grounds collapsed like shattered mirrors, golden runes exploding into countless fireflies across the sky. Chen Ji stood at the heart of chaos, the fragment in his hand reconstructing itself with almost maddening fervor—those fragmented strokes reshaping under the nourishment of bloodline, the severed connections healing under the guidance of spiritual consciousness. He felt an unprecedented power surge through his body, as if countless streams were converging into a vast ocean. The gaze of the Heavenly Dao's Eye remained scorching, yet within that tremor emerged a hint of... wariness? 'Good.' Chen Ji murmured, a cold smile curling his lips. 'Since the rules must break, let them shatter completely.' He raised his head, his gaze piercing through the barriers of the Forbidden Grounds toward the direction of the Imperial Capital—a passage at the convergence of the Three Realms was tearing open a chasm vast enough to devour heaven and earth.

Dark clouds like ink churned above the Imperial Capital, forming an inverted mountain. The city's common people were already panic-stricken, kneeling on the ground and kowtowing to pray to the sky, unaware that the source of this catastrophe was a Servant Disciple they had never even glanced at. On the city tower, several high officials of the dynasty stood with ashen faces, gazing at the fissure—expanding visibly, as if a slumbering giant was awakening. 'Three Realms Convergence...' a white-haired elder trembled, 'This is a phenomenon from ancient myths! Legend says every convergence signifies the reshaping of heavenly and earthly laws...' Before his words ended, a golden light shot from the depths of the fissure, illuminating the entire Imperial Capital.

dialogue.content: Three Realms Convergence, heaven and earth mourn together. This moment, I have waited far too long.

text.content: Chen Ji stood in the void, behind him the crumbling Forbidden Grounds, before him the passage of Three Realms Convergence. His figure seemed insignificant in the golden light, yet possessed an undeniable presence. The complete version of the Tianji Record had appeared in his palm, those words no longer vague symbols but a complete scroll of destiny—chessboard, chesspieces, the Chess Player, everything perfectly clear. He drew a deep breath, raised his right hand, and traced a mysterious trajectory through the void. In that instant, the Three Realms passage fully opened.

On the other side of the passage, the demonic army stood ready. Demon Path Commander Ye Qing stood atop her war chariot, her veil blown by the wild wind, revealing a treacherous yet stunningly beautiful face. When she witnessed the passage opening, her lips curved slightly upward. 'He truly did it.' she murmured softly, then gestured. 'Transmit orders—all forces respond! Today, we shall show those self-righteous hypocrites what true power really is!' The demonic army surged into the passage like a black tide. Meanwhile, envoys from the dynasty also arrived, standing atop the city tower with complex expressions as they gazed at all this.

The forces from the three great sects finally made their belated appearance. The elders of the Tianqing Sect wore grim expressions, never imagining that the Servant Disciple deemed worthless could cause such a massive upheaval. Han Lie, the number one genius of Xuanwu Sect, stood at the very front of the crowd, fury burning in his eyes. 'Chen Ji!' he ground out through clenched teeth, 'You despicable wretch, how dare you do such a thing!' Yet faced with that fissure capable of tearing apart heaven and earth, even someone as arrogantly defiant as him dared not act rashly. At this moment, the gazes of the entire world converged on the Three Realms Convergence—and all eyes ultimately fell upon that solitary figure standing alone in the void.

dialogue.content: Distinguished ones, you have waited long. Today, the final stage of this ancient chess game shall be concluded by me, Chen Ji.

text.content: Chen Ji's voice echoed between heaven and earth, clearly reaching every listener's ear. He did not deliberately raise his volume, yet possessed an almost magical quality that compelled everyone to listen. 'Ancient chess game?' Han Lie coldly laughed, 'Atrash like you also speaks of an ancient chess game?' Chen Ji did not look at him, his gaze sweeping across everyone present—demons, orthodox, dynasty, representatives of three forces gathered together, yet each harboring their own calculations. 'I know what you're thinking.' Chen Ji calmly said, 'The demons want to invade the Three Realms, the orthodox want to maintain order, the dynasty wants to remain uninvolved. Unfortunately, you are all wrong.' He raised the Tianji Record in his hand, golden light illuminating the entire sky.

Chen Ji drew a deep breath, knowing the next words would determine the fate of the entire Three Realms. 'I give you three choices.' His voice was calm, yet carried undeniable power. 'The first path—become a vessel.' He pointed to his own chest. 'I merge with Cang Yutian, trading my sole existence for permanent peace in the Three Realms. This path is simplest, yet most humiliating—I will lose all consciousness, becoming part of the Heavenly Dao's will, and you will continue as chesspieces, eternally bound.' The crowd erupted in uproar, never expecting Chen Ji to propose such a plan.

'The second path—annihilate everything.' A cold light flickered in Chen Ji's eyes. 'Including the Heavenly Dao, the Chess Player, and the entire chess game, returning the Three Realms to primordial chaos. This path is most satisfying, yet most cruel—all living beings will turn to nothingness, all civilizations will be reduced to ash. You may resist, but the outcome was long since determined.' His tone grew increasingly cold. 'The third path—shatter the rules.' He fiercely gripped the Tianji Record, golden light surging violently. 'Create an entirely new system of destiny, allowing everyone to become master of their own fate. This path is hardest, yet brightest—however, the price is we must stake everything.'

choice.prompt: Three paths lie before you, the ancient chess game is about to conclude—how will you declare your ultimate choice?

text.content: Chen Ji's voice echoed between heaven and earth, each word carrying irresistible power. 'I choose the third path.' He raised the Tianji Record, golden light surging violently, as if about to tear apart the entire sky. 'The Heavenly Dao as chess, all beings as pieces—this ends now.' The words fell, and the Three Realms passage violently trembled, as if some terrifying existence was awakening.

However, just as he prepared to take that step, a razor-sharp sword light cleaved through the void—Su Qingyao had somehow arrived, her eyes brimming with determination. 'Chen Ji, you dare not!'

text.content: "Path Two." A flash of madness flickered in Chen Ji's eyes. "Since this chess game was fundamentally wrong from the start, why not tear it all down and start over?" His voice was ice-cold, devoid of any emotion. "Chaos begins anew, everything reshaped—that is true fairness." As his words fell, the entire Three Realms passage began to violently tremble, as if the bell of doomsday had already rung.

choices.memory_label: 选择了毁灭一切的极端道路

text.content: Just as everyone was in shock, the sky suddenly darkened. A massive eye emerged from the depths of the crack—it had no whites, only profound darkness and burning purple flames within. The Heavenly Dao's Eye—it could no longer hold back, revealing itself in person. "Chen Ji." That voice seemed to come from all directions, yet simultaneously rang directly in everyone's minds. "You think that fragment in your hands can oppose me?" Chen Ji stared directly at that giant eye, showing not a trace of fear. "No." Hecalmly承认, "But I have never been alone." His gaze swept across Ye Qing, Han Lie, the three great sect masters, the imperial court officials—each and every one was a piece on his chessboard, yet also part of his grand design.

dialogue.content: You think they will help you? Foolish. All beings are my chess pieces. Since ancient times, no one has ever broken free.
Is that so? And what about piece number forty-nine? That piece you arranged to monitor me by your side—do you think I didn't know of its existence?

text.content: The Heavenly Dao's Eye visibly trembled—this was the first time it had shown a crack before Chen Ji. "You..." Chen Ji didn't give it a chance to finish. Instead, he fiercely hurled the Tianji Record into the void. The fragment expanded in mid-air, transforming into a massive scroll of destiny. Countless points of light flickered across its surface, each representing a chess piece—with the forty-ninth one, uniquely radiant, steadily growing brighter. "Hidden for three thousand years—aren't you exhausted?" Chen Ji's voice cut like ice. "Now, it's time for you to emerge." The entire Three Realms passage froze in absolute stillness, as if time itself had ceased to flow.

On the scroll, the light point numbered forty-nine began to expand. At first it was merely a speck of dust, then a grain of sand, then a fragment of stone—it kept growing, eventually forming a vague humanoid shape. That shape had no face, only a pair of tightly closed eyes. But the moment Chen Ji's words fell, those eyes slowly opened. Purple light burst forth from them—not the oppressive radiance of the Heavenly Dao's Eye, but a deeper, more ancient light. That light swept across everyone present, and each person felt a pang of terror—as if something far more terrifying than the Heavenly Dao was gazing upon them.

Chen Ji静静地注视着 the opened eyes, yet his heart churned with tumultuous waves. He knew piece forty-nine was no simple matter, but he never anticipated—that its existence wasn't even recorded in the complete Tianji Record. This was the only blind spot in his grand design, his greatest variable. Yet he did not retreat; instead, meeting that gaze, he revealed a deeply meaningful smile. "Finally willing to wake?" His voice was calm, yet carried an odd sense of familiarity. "I thought I'd have to wait until the end of time." Those purple eyes flickered, as if responding to Chen Ji's words. In the next instant, a voice sounded—not from the scroll, but directly in everyone's mind.

"Chen Ji." That voice was ancient and distant, as if traversing countless ages. "You have finally arrived." Chen Ji raised an eyebrow, saying nothing. The voice continued: "Three thousand years ago, I placed my final chess piece here. I thought I would await a destined inheritor, but never expected—the one who came was a madman who defies heaven's designs." Upon hearing this, Chen Ji's lips curved into a cold smile. "Madman? Interesting." He raised his hand, and the Tianji Record's radiance surged anew. "Since you think I'm a madman, let me show you—just how far a madman can go."

"Since you've waited three thousand years, surely it wasn't to speak such nonsense." His voice carried a hint of playfulness. "Speak—what do you want?" Those purple eyes flickered, as ifscrutinizinging Chen Ji. After a moment, an ancient laughter rang out: "Interesting... truly interesting."

text.content: "Enough." Chen Ji's voice turned cold, "Stop your tricks. What are you, and why are you in the Tianji Record? Speak!" His momentum surged like a rainbow, and the golden light of the Tianji Record formed a massive phantom behind him—the lingering shadows of the Tianji Record's past masters, vague yet carrying a terrifying pressure. Those purple eyes finally truly looked at Chen Ji, the ancient laughter turning into a low hum. "What's the rush... you'll know soon enough."

choices.description: Whatever the 49th piece represents, the greatest enemy is the Eye of Heavenly Dao. Join forces to eliminate the threat first.
choices.visible_reward: Gain powerful allies, poised to reverse the situation
choices.risk_hint: Raising a tiger will bring disaster—the 49th piece may prove more dangerous than the Heavenly Dao itself

text.content: Chen Ji turned around, facing the Eye of Heavenly Dao directly. "Whatever your origins—" He raised the Tianji Record, golden light blazing, "We share a common enemy." The purple eyes flickered, as if in contemplation. A moment later, an ancient voice rang out: "Interesting... you wish to ally with me?" Chen Ji sneered: "Not an alliance—a transaction. What you want, I can provide." Those purple eyes finally opened fully, revealing a knowing smile. "Deal."

dialogue.content: Three thousand years of planning, five hundred lifetimes of reincarnation, countless calculations of heavenly secrets... all answers point to this very moment.

text.content: The moment Chen Ji's words fell, the entire Three Realms passage underwent a violent transformation. The suspended chess pieces began to move, golden, wood, water, fire, and earth-colored lights converging into a brilliant river of stars, encircling Chen Ji, the 49th piece, and the Eye of Heavenly Dao. This was the ultimate form of the Chess Game of Eternity—the Chess Player and the pieces, the Heavenly Dao and those who defy it, all clearly presented beneath the same sky for the first time. "It has begun." Chen Ji murmured, "The Chess Game of Eternity, the final match—begins now."

The Eye of Heavenly Dao let out a roar of fury, purple lightning bursting from its deep pupils, striking toward Chen Ji and the 49th piece. However, the lightning was blocked mid-air by an invisible barrier—the power of the 49th piece, ancient and mysterious, as if from the chaos before the world's creation. "You've finally arrived." The 49th piece's voice rang out, ancient and distant, "The main body of the Destiny Writer." Chen Ji's heart trembled at these words—Destiny Writer? That was a being from legend, even older than the Heavenly Dao, said to have created the first Tianji Record and the first to introduce the concept of "destiny" into the Three Realms. If the 49th piece was the main body of the Destiny Writer... then the Tianji Record in his hands...

Just then, Mo Xiansheng's voice sounded in Chen Ji's mind—his first time actively contacting Chen Ji. "Young master." The voice carried a rare gravity, "Matters are far more complex than you imagine. The 49th piece is indeed the main body of the Destiny Writer, but it is not complete—it is merely a strand of consciousness split off by the Heavenly Dao. Three thousand years ago, the Destiny Writer attempted to break the Heavenly Dao's rules, but was counterattacked, its consciousness shattered into countless fragments scattered across the Three Realms." Chen Ji furrowed his brow: "And the Tianji Record?" Mo Xiansheng was silent for a moment before slowly saying: "The Tianji Record... is the core of those fragments."

Chen Ji took a deep breath, processing this shocking information. He looked at those purple eyes, his gaze gaining new complexity. The Eye of Heavenly Dao was an enemy—this was certain. But what about the 49th piece? It was a fragment of the Destiny Writer, a being betrayed by the Heavenly Dao, with a common enemy as Chen Ji. But could it truly be trusted? A being that could even betray itself... "What are you thinking?" The 49th piece's voice rang out, as if seeing through Chen Ji's thoughts, "Rest assured, I bear no goodwill toward the Heavenly Dao. Back then, it split and imprisoned me—this debt, I will collect personally." Chen Ji sneered: "Words are cheap." The 49th piece was silent for a moment, then said something that left Chen Ji completely stunned:

The words struck like thunder in Chen Ji's mind. His father—Chen Xuan, the previous inheritor of the Tianji Record, a being erased by the Heavenly Dao three thousand years ago. The 49th piece actually knew his father? "You..." Chen Ji's voice tightened, "You knew my father?" The 49th piece's purple eyes flickered, as if recalling something distant. "More than knew." Its voice carried complex emotions, "Back then, those who attempted to break the Heavenly Dao's rules were not just the Destiny Writer—there was also your father. They were partners, and also..." The 49th piece paused, "Close friends."

Chen Ji's heart was churning with huge waves, but his expression remained as calm as still water. "So what?" His voice was cold, "Are you trying to move me with my father?" The 49th piece shook its head. "No, I am merely stating facts." Its voice became solemn, "Three thousand years ago, your father, at the cost of his life, sealed the seed of the Tianji Record into your bloodline. And I was split into countless fragments, sealed within the Tianji Record, waiting for someone who could reunite everything." It paused, "That person, is you." Chen Ji sneered: "Why should I believe you?" The 49th piece's purple eyes stared directly at him, "Because you are Chen Xuan's son. You have arranged the Three Realms, calculated all living beings, yet never truly trusted anyone—but you will trust your father."

Chen Ji fell silent. He thought of the words his father left behind, the fragments hidden within the scattered pages, and the mysterious yet magnificent figure described by Mo Xiansheng. If his father truly collaborated with the Destiny Writer, then the chess game he arranged... from the very beginning, was never a game for one person alone. "Very well." Chen Ji finally spoke, his voice still calm, "I will暂且 believe you for now. But remember—" He raised the Tianji Record, golden light blazing, "If you dare betray me, I will let you know what it means to wish for death rather than life." The 49th piece let out a low laugh. "Indeed, Chen Xuan's son." It said, "Then—let us begin. Eye of Heavenly Dao, I have waited for this day for three thousand years."

The Eye of Heavenly Dao seemed to sense the threat. The massive pupil began to contract violently, purple flames burning wildly within. "You think your alliance can oppose me?" The voice carried boundless fury, "Ridiculous! Three thousand years of planning, I have calculated everything—including your alliance!" As the words fell, the Three Realms passage shook violently. Countless black chains shot forth from the depths of the cracks, coiling around Chen Ji and the 49th piece. At the same time, those suspended chess pieces began to spin madly, forming a massive cage. "This is... the Heavenly Fate Prison!" the 49th piece exclaimed, "It knew all along we would ally!" Chen Ji sneered: "So what if it knew?" He raised the Tianji Record, golden light blazing, "I arrange the Three Realms, never expecting my opponents to be ignorant—I only need them to know, and still be unable to stop me!"
